note: Machine copy of the family catalog. compile_spec.py resolves every `catalog:` key against this file; tests/test_catalog_sync.py fails when this file and the prose diverge. Keys are `<section>/<row>`: tasks/<kind>, families/<name>, blocks/<type>, defaults/<decision>. Beyond §1-§4: `metric_direction` mirrors family-catalog.md §6, `fork_order` §5, `admission` §7, and `inspection` is the machine copy of references/inspect-contract.md §3-§4 (views, targets, links, limits).

graph_level.note: a graph sample adds no task kind: at level node the task rows apply unchanged (every node is a row with the partition's label); at level graph these kinds keep head, loss and metrics but require sample_shape graph with a graph_id and a graph_pool block before the head (compiler rule W2)

binary.loss_notes: + pos_weight when the minority share < 0.3 (analysis:F<n> on imbalance)

multiclass.loss_notes: + class weights or label smoothing 0.05 when imbalanced

multilabel.when: several binary labels, carried as one shaped column of delimited class names

label.form: one shaped column holding a delimited set of class names per row ("a|c"); the empty string is the empty set

multilabel.breakdown: pr_auc per label (the per-label list); pr_auc_macro is its scalar

regression.loss_notes: huber when the analysis found outliers in the label, else mse

ordinal.loss_notes: cumulative logits from a rank-consistent head: one shared score and k-1 ordered thresholds, so P(y > j) = sigma(z_j) decreases in j and every class probability is non-negative

unsupervised.recon_dim: n_numeric + the sum of the cardinalities of the embedded nominals (a one-hot nominal is numeric columns): the numeric columns are reconstructed as values, each embedded nominal as logits over its categories
unsupervised.loss_notes: the backend's mixed loss: mse on numeric columns + cross_entropy on embedded nominals

anomaly.when: a rare label the user declares an anomaly, or no label with --goal anomaly
anomaly.recon_dim: as unsupervised, under the reconstruction and vae losses; z under svdd
anomaly.loss_notes: reconstruction, or svdd for the one-class hypersphere (the centre is a buffer of the model, saved with the weights)

sequence-classification.when: analysis:context.time exists, the shaper's split is time, windows are declared

sequence-regression.when: analysis:context.time exists, the shaper's split is time, windows are declared

forecast.when: a horizon is declared on a windowed sample with a time split

base_kind.values: a key of sequence_map whose value is task.kind
base_kind.note: the effective kind every reader of the base uses (head, loss, metrics, readout, serving reading); forecast's base is regression

classes.note: ordered for ordinal; the label names for multilabel

label_format.default: names when the label column holds strings, else index; multilabel is delimited with sep '|'

positive.note: the class that means positive (binary) or anomalous (anomaly); for a binary task it must be task.classes[1] (T1e refuses classes[0]: list the positive class second)

anomaly_rate.values: a number in (0, 1), with its own source in anomaly_rate_source (user: or analysis:)
anomaly_rate.note: optional: the expected share of anomalous rows; /vega-eval reads it for an unlabelled anomaly task (precision_at_k's k, the threshold's valid quantile); a labelled task takes the train part's positive share instead

selection_rule: metrics.selection.monitor is always valid.<primary>; early_stopping.monitor defaults to the same (a loss-monitored early stop is an alternative to offer, not the default, because the loss and the metric can disagree under class weighting)

mlp-plain.when: tabular rows, input_dim <= ~200, analysis:importance learnable, no time context
mlp-plain.composition: [embedding?] -> concat -> (dense -> activation -> dropout) x depth -> head

mlp-residual.when: as mlp-plain with depth >= 3, or blueprint:posture says neural on a non-linear importance
mlp-residual.composition: [embedding?] -> concat -> dense(width) -> residual(inner: dense -> batchnorm|layernorm -> activation -> dropout) x depth -> head

ft-transformer.when: wide tabular (input_dim > ~50) or many high-cardinality nominals; the user accepts the cost
ft-transformer.nominals: the feature_tokenizer reads the nominal columns itself (one token per nominal from its own table); an embedding before it is refused (compiler rule G2)

cnn1d.when: sample.shape = window, local temporal patterns (short windows, regular sampling per analysis:context.time)
cnn1d.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> (conv1d -> activation -> pool1d) x depth -> flatten -> dense -> head

gru.when: windows with long dependencies, irregular patterns, forecast
gru.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> gru(hidden, num_layers, return: last) -> head; return: all -> pool(mean) or attention(pool) are defaults/recurrent_return's alternatives (the steps pooled, or self-attended then pooled)

lstm.when: windows with long dependencies, irregular patterns, forecast
lstm.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> lstm(hidden, num_layers, return: last) -> head; return: all -> pool(mean) or attention(pool) are defaults/recurrent_return's alternatives (the steps pooled, or self-attended then pooled)

transformer-seq.when: long windows, many series, budget allows
transformer-seq.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> dense(d) -> positional -> transformer_encoder(d, L) -> pool(mean) -> head

autoencoder.when: unsupervised / anomaly; reconstruction as the objective
autoencoder.composition: [embedding?] -> concat -> sequential(dense x depth) -> dense(z) -> decoder(widths reversed) -> head(recon_dim, none)
alternatives: vae when a generative reading is wanted

vae.when: as autoencoder with a latent prior
vae.composition: [embedding?] -> concat -> sequential(dense x depth) -> dense(2z) -> reparameterize(z) -> decoder -> head(recon_dim, none)

deep-svdd.when: one-class anomaly with a hypersphere objective
deep-svdd.composition: [embedding?] -> concat -> sequential(dense x depth) -> head(z, none, bias: false)

linear.when: the sanity floor every supervised campaign includes as an ablation, on every sample shape
linear.composition: row: [embedding?] -> concat -> head; window: [embedding?] -> concat -> flatten -> head; graph, level node: [embedding?] -> concat -> head (structure-blind: each node's own features); graph, level graph: [embedding?] -> concat -> graph_pool(mean) -> head

pca-floor.when: the floor for unsupervised / anomaly: a linear autoencoder, PCA by another name

rnn.when: a sequence task (sample.shape = window); the ablation floor for the recurrent families - what gru / lstm must beat
rnn.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> rnn(hidden, num_layers, return: last) -> dropout -> head

bi-lstm.when: classification of complete windows where the whole window, its future included, is legitimately visible at inference; never forecast, never serving.mode stream (compiler rule W3: ERROR)
bi-lstm.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> lstm(hidden, num_layers, bidirectional: true, return: last) -> dropout -> head

bi-gru.when: classification of complete windows where the whole window, its future included, is legitimately visible at inference; never forecast, never serving.mode stream (compiler rule W3: ERROR)
bi-gru.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> gru(hidden, num_layers, bidirectional: true, return: last) -> dropout -> head

lstm-attention.when: long windows where the informative step is not the last one
lstm-attention.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> lstm(hidden, num_layers, return: all) -> attention_pool(hidden) -> dropout -> head

gru-attention.when: long windows where the informative step is not the last one
gru-attention.composition: [embedding -> concat]? -> gru(hidden, num_layers, return: all) -> attention_pool(hidden) -> dropout -> head

gcn.when: an edges part exists (manifest.outputs.files.edges, from the shaper's graph_edges step) and the analysis found the rows related (a relations / segments / spatial finding) - the family blueprint:posture names, or the vega:default graph family when the posture says graph
gcn.composition: [edge_dropout]? -> [embedding -> concat]? -> [gcn_conv -> activation -> dropout] x depth -> head at level node; ... -> graph_pool(mean) -> head at level graph
alternatives: graphsage (inductive, neighbour sampling - when the graph is large)

graphsage.when: the inductive protocol on a large graph (neighbour sampling instead of the full adjacency), or heterophilous neighbourhoods where the root's own features must survive the aggregation
graphsage.composition: [edge_dropout]? -> [embedding -> concat]? -> [sage_conv -> activation -> dropout] x depth -> head (+ graph_pool(mean) before the head at level graph)

gat.when: neighbour importance varies - some edges matter, most do not
gat.composition: [edge_dropout]? -> [embedding -> concat]? -> [gat_conv(heads: 8, concat: true) -> activation -> dropout] x (depth - 1) -> gat_conv(heads: 1, concat: false) -> head (+ graph_pool(mean) before the head at level graph)

gin.when: level graph - the most discriminative aggregation for graph-level tasks (injective sum)
gin.composition: [edge_dropout]? -> [embedding -> concat]? -> [gin_conv -> activation -> dropout] x depth -> graph_pool(sum) -> head

serving.mode.online: a stated latency makes ft-transformer and transformer-seq a FORK: quoting the latency (source blueprint:serving)
serving.mode.stream: requires a windowed sample, so only the sequence families apply

family_forces.posture: blueprint:posture names a family or a family class (linear / tree / neural / none yet); tree or none-yet is overruled only with a user: source or a vega:default quoting the posture's forces
family_forces.edges_part: a graph family (sample_shape graph) requires manifest.outputs.files.edges, a declared sample.protocol and graph_pool iff level == graph (compiler rule W2); a non-graph family on a graph shape is a WARN (the edges are ignored, said so)
family_forces.bidirectional: a bidirectional recurrent block on a forecast task or a stream serving mode is an ERROR (compiler rule W3): it reads the window's future
family_forces.fork: the architecture fork names graph families only when an edges part exists and the recurrent variants (rnn, bi-*, *-attention) only when the sample shape is window

admission.note: the closed definition of complete coverage: one cell is (family, sample shape, graph level, effective task), plus the named variants; a task written kind/base is a sequence-* kind over that base; anomaly is run with and without a label
not_admitted: a reconstruction family (autoencoder, vae, pca-floor, deep-svdd) on window or graph
a graph family on unsupervised or anomaly
bi-lstm or bi-gru on forecast or under serving.mode stream (W3)
any window family on a split that is not time (W1)

dense.notes: activation may be a separate activation block instead

concat.shape_rule: joins the numeric features and every embedding output
concat.notes: required after embedding; alternatives: [] with the rationale 'structural'

batchnorm.notes: needs batch >= 8; the compiler warns below 32

dropout.notes: inactive at eval; the layer shows where it sits

residual.shape_rule: x + f(x); projection: auto inserts a dense when widths differ
residual.notes: the compiler checks inner keeps the width or the projection is present

sequential.shape_rule: the chain of its inner blocks' rules

parallel.shape_rule: every branch sees the input; concat sums the widths, sum requires equal widths

rnn.shape_rule: (N, L, F) -> (N, H*dirs) for last/mean/max, (N, L, H*dirs) for all
rnn.notes: plain Elman RNN (torch.nn.RNN); gradients vanish on long L, which is why gru / lstm are the default recurrent blocks and rnn is the ablation floor; return: mean and max are pooled over the steps inside the block

params.num_layers: int (default 1; `layers` is the same param under its old name)

gru.shape_rule: (B, L, F) -> (B, hidden*dirs) for last/mean/max, (B, L, hidden*dirs) for all
gru.notes: return replaces any implicit 'last step' behaviour; a spec without it means last. bidirectional: true is subject to W3 (never forecast, never stream); return: mean and max are pooled over the steps inside the block

params.num_layers: int (default 1; `layers` is the same param under its old name)

lstm.shape_rule: (B, L, F) -> (B, hidden*dirs) for last/mean/max, (B, L, hidden*dirs) for all
lstm.notes: return replaces any implicit 'last step' behaviour; a spec without it means last. bidirectional: true is subject to W3 (never forecast, never stream); return: mean and max are pooled over the steps inside the block

attention.shape_rule: (B, L, d) -> (B, d) when pool: true, else (B, L, d)

attention_pool.notes: one learned query attends over the L steps - a pooling readout, the one the *-attention families use after return: all; alpha = softmax_t(q . tanh(W h_t + b)), y = sum_t alpha_t h_t; attention mixes the steps among themselves, attention_pool only weighs them

feature_tokenizer.shape_rule: rows -> (B, n_numeric + n_nominal + 1, d) with a [cls] token
feature_tokenizer.notes: FT-Transformer entry; one token per numeric column (x_j * w_j + b_j) and one per nominal column from its own table, so the tokenizer reads the nominals itself and no embedding block precedes it (compiler rule G2)

head.notes: exactly one per spec unless multilabel heads are declared; `out` and the activation are forced by the task row, so the catalog marks the head structural and `alternatives: []` is legal with the rationale saying what forces it; `bias` (default true) is false in deep-svdd, where a bias lets the hypersphere collapse; on an ordinal task the backend builds the rank-consistent cumulative head: one shared score and out = k-1 ordered thresholds

decoder.shape_rule: (B, z) -> (B, out), out defaulting to input_dim
decoder.notes: autoencoders; widths default to the encoder's dense widths reversed; the reconstruction head (recon_dim) follows it

gcn_conv.notes: D^-1/2 (A+I) D^-1/2 X W (sym) or D^-1 (A+I) X W (rw); an edge weight (the edges part's weight column) multiplies the messages and enters the degree; takes the node features plus the edge index; graph shape only

sage_conv.notes: W1 x_i + W2 agg_{j in N(i)} x_j, the root kept apart from its neighbours; an edge weight multiplies the messages; the block neighbour sampling applies to (sample.neighbours[k] for the k-th conv); takes the node features plus the edge index; graph shape only

gat_conv.shape_rule: (N, F) + (E) -> (N, out*heads) when concat, else (N, out) (heads averaged)
gat_conv.notes: attention coefficients per edge (LeakyReLU, softmax over N(i)); an edge weight multiplies alpha_ij after the softmax, without renormalising; attn_dropout drops coefficients, not features; takes the node features plus the edge index; graph shape only

gin_conv.notes: MLP((1+eps) x_i + sum_{j in N(i)} x_j) - the injective sum aggregation; an edge weight multiplies the messages; takes the node features plus the edge index; graph shape only

graph_pool.notes: groups nodes by sample.graph_id into G graphs (the batch's graph_index); allowed only at level graph, and required there (W2)

edge_dropout.notes: drops edges, not features; training only (identity at eval); the kept edges replace the graph for every later block of the same forward pass

custom.shape_rule: the declared out_shape, checked by the smoke pass
custom.notes: user: source only; marked unverified in the layer; code_ref names a module under the campaign root (custom/<id>.py) that the emitter copies into <model>/custom/<stem>.py, where the builder resolves it

blocks_coverage_note: the catalog names every block type of the grammar; which of them a backend implements is that backend's coverage.json (`blocks`, with `planned` for the ones it lists as not built yet). compile_spec.py's B2 refuses a block the named backend does not list, and names it planned when the backend's `planned.blocks` carries it

sizing.default: width clip(2*input_dim, 32, 256) rounded to a power of two, raised one step when the analysis found non-linear importance; depth 2 below 1000 training rows, 3 below 100000, 4 above; transformers d = clip(width/2, 32, 128), L = depth-1; RNN hidden = width/2; CNN channels width/4 -> width/2; bottleneck z = dims_95 from geometry:space
sizing.because: parameters scale with the rows the chain has and the input width, not with fashion
sizing.alternative: x2 / /2 width and +-1 depth as capacity rungs

optimizer.default: adamw lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4, betas (0.9, 0.999) - tabular; lr 1e-4 for transformers; sgd momentum 0.9 lr 1e-2 only as an ablation
optimizer.because: robust across widths without tuning; decoupled decay
optimizer.alternative: sgd for generalisation ablations; any optimizer the backend's coverage.json lists by name

schedule.default: cosine with warmup_epochs = 3 when max_epochs >= 30; plateau (factor 0.5, patience 5) otherwise
schedule.because: warmup steadies AdamW's first steps; cosine needs a known horizon
schedule.alternative: onecycle when a max lr was found by a range test; none as an ablation

batch_size.default: clip(rows_train / 8, 16, 512) rounded to a power of two
batch_size.because: ~8 optimizer steps per epoch at minimum, so an epoch means something
batch_size.alternative: x2 / /2 ablations; the smoke panel shows memory per batch

max_epochs.default: 200 with early stopping; budget.wall_clock_min from the user or 20
max_epochs.because: early stopping ends it; the budget bounds a run that never converges

early_stopping.default: monitor valid.<primary>, patience 10 (max_epochs / 20, >= 5), min_delta 1e-3, restore best
early_stopping.because: the primary metric is what selection uses
early_stopping.alternative: patience 20 on noisy valid metrics; monitor valid.loss

init.default: kaiming_uniform for relu-family, xavier_uniform for tanh/sigmoid, zeros bias; embeddings N(0, 0.1)

dropout.default: 0.1 (mlp-plain), 0.2 (mlp-residual), 0.1 (transformers), 0.1 after a recurrent readout (rnn, bi-*, *-attention); 0 in the linear ablation
dropout.because: the widths above vs the training rows the chain has
dropout.alternative: 0.3-0.5 when train >> valid (an analysis:F<n> on size, or a training diagnostic)

normalisation.default: batchnorm in MLP blocks when batch >= 32, else layernorm; layernorm in transformers and RNN outputs
normalisation.because: batch statistics are unreliable on small batches

weight_decay.because: mild shrinkage; the analysis's overfitting finding raises it

grad_clip.because: a cheap guard against the NaN epoch; the pre-clip norm is recorded in the epoch record's grad_norm

precision.default: fp32; bf16 autocast only with --device cuda and the user's word

seed.default: 7 (the chain's), and the data loader order seeded too

imbalance.default: pos_weight / class weights = inverse frequency clipped to 10
imbalance.because: keeps the gradient of the minority alive without exploding it
imbalance.alternative: focal loss; resampling is the shaper's business, not the trainer's

device.default: device: auto (cuda -> mps -> cpu), num_workers: 0, precision: fp32
device.because: a run must be reproducible where it is read, and a worker pool changes batch order unless seeded

embedding_dim.default: min(50, round(1.6 * cardinality^0.56)), rounded to an even number
embedding_dim.because: sub-linear in the cardinality, capped so a rare nominal does not dominate the input width
embedding_dim.alternative: /2 when train >> valid; a one-hot encode in the shaper when cardinality <= 8

graph_protocol.default: inductive: the reference graph is the train nodes and the edges among them; a valid node is a query that receives messages from reference nodes only (never from another query), and the test nodes and every edge touching one enter through the seal at /vega-eval, as queries the same way
graph_protocol.because: keeps the test seal's meaning - no test row is seen, as a feature or as a neighbour, before /vega-eval
graph_protocol.alternative: transductive (user: source only, exposure.kind features in the layer) when the deployment graph is fixed and the unlabeled nodes are legitimately present at training time

graph_depth.because: over-smoothing beyond 2-3 hops on homophilous graphs - every node's representation converges to the same one
graph_depth.alternative: 3 with residual connections (residual around each conv)

recurrent_return.default: last for classification and regression; all -> attention_pool when the windows are long (the *-attention families)
recurrent_return.because: the last state summarises a short window; over a long one the informative step is anywhere, and a learned readout finds it

bidirectional.because: forecast and stream serving forbid the future - a bidirectional block reads it (W3)
bidirectional.alternative: true for classification of complete windows (the bi-* families)

window_context.default: previous-part: an anchor's length-1 context rows may come from the previous part of the same series (train before valid, valid before test), so every valid and test row is scored
window_context.because: every valid and test row gets a prediction; the context rows are inputs the deployment also has
window_context.alternative: none: drop the first length-1 rows of each series in each part and count them unscored

window_series.default: the lag step's group_by, else the split's by, else null
window_series.because: a window that crosses two series mixes two processes
window_series.unattended_warn: windows may cross series — no series key in the shaping record

autoregressive.default: true for forecast (the target's rows up to the anchor are one more input channel), false otherwise
autoregressive.because: a forecast without the target's own past discards the strongest predictor

graph_batching.default: graphs at level graph; else full when the training view has at most 200 000 nodes and 5 000 000 edges; else sampled with neighbours [25, 10] (graphsage's)
graph_batching.because: full-batch gradients are exact and cheapest while the graph fits

points.when: sample.shape window and the shaping record names no series key (no lag group_by, no split by)
points.unattended: null, with WARN: windows may cross series — no series key in the shaping record
always inductive: never asked unattended, because transductive needs a user: turn (W2)

metric_direction_note: family-catalog.md §6: the direction in which a metric is better, for every metric the backends implement plus the training loss; a per-unit metric (f1_per_class, per_feature_error, per_horizon_error) is read element-wise; none marks a descriptive reading that has no better direction and is never a selection metric

inductive.meaning: the training graph is the train (and valid) nodes and the edges among them only; the test nodes and every edge touching one enter through the seal at /vega-eval

transductive.meaning: the test nodes' features and their edges are in the graph during training while their labels stay sealed

layernorm.formula: y = γ·(x − mean x)/√(var x + ε) + β
layernorm.recompute: the formula over the sample = out

conv1d.formula: y[t,o] = b[o] + Σ_c Σ_k W[o,c,k]·x[t·s+k−p, c]

pool1d.recompute: the pooling formula over in = out

rnn.recompute: the step-by-step unroll = the module's sequence output

gru.formula: r,z = σ(…) ; n = tanh(W_in·x+b_in + r⊙(W_hn·h+b_hn)) ; h_t = (1−z)⊙n + z⊙h_{t−1}
gru.recompute: the step-by-step unroll = the module's sequence output

lstm.formula: i,f,o = σ(…) ; g = tanh(…) ; c_t = f⊙c_{t−1} + i⊙g ; h_t = o⊙tanh(c_t)
lstm.recompute: the step-by-step unroll = the module's sequence output

attention.formula: A_h = softmax(Q_h K_hᵀ/√d_h) ; y = W_o·[A_1 V_1 ; … ; A_H V_H]
attention.recompute: the recomputed attention over in = out

attention_pool.formula: α = softmax_t(q·tanh(W h_t + b)) ; y = Σ_t α_t h_t

transformer_encoder.formula: x ← x + MHA(LN₁ x) ; x ← x + FF(LN₂ x)

feature_tokenizer.formula: T_j = x_j·W_j + b_j ; tokens = [cls ; T_1 … T_n]
feature_tokenizer.recompute: the token formula over in = out

pool.recompute: the pooling formula over in = out

head.formula: z = W·x + b ; ordinal: z_j = w·x + θ_j with θ_0 ≥ θ_1 ≥ …

decoder.formula: x̂ = W_k·act(… act(W_1 z + b_1) …) + b_k

reparameterize.formula: z = μ at inference ; KL = −½ Σ (1 + log σ² − μ² − σ²)

gcn_conv.recompute: Σ_j coef·W h_j + b at the target = out

sage_conv.recompute: root + aggregate at the target = out

gat_conv.formula: α_ij = softmax_j(LeakyReLU(a_srcᵀ W h_j + a_dstᵀ W h_i)) ; h'_i = ‖_h Σ_j α^h_ij W^h h_j
gat_conv.recompute: the heads of Σ_j α·W h_j at the target = out

graph_pool.recompute: the readout over the graph's nodes = out

input.formula: x = the shaped inputs (numeric, nominal ids, edges)

parallel_merge.recompute: concat or sum of the branches = out

encoder_layer.formula: x ← x + MHA(LN₁ x) ; x ← x + FF(LN₂ x)
encoder_layer.recompute: x + MHA(LN₁ x), then + FF(LN₂ ·) = out

sigmoid_each.formula: p_k = σ(z_k), each label on its own

horizon.formula: ŷ_{t+h} = z_h, h = 1…H (quantile loss: z_{h,q}, horizon-major)

binary_logit.scalar: sign·z, sign +1 for the positive class and −1 for the other

binary.default_pick: the class predicted at the threshold

multilabel.default_pick: the label of the largest σ

numbers.rule: num(v) = float(f'{float(v):.9g}'), which round-trips float32 exactly; NaN and infinities are refused
